# Match Confidence — how much to trust a fingerprint hit

> ⚠️ **Status: In Review — awaiting Human Operator approval** (Constitution Art. II).
> 
> From the ecosystem-survey half of the report. ⭐ **The only item in the entire report that improves matching QUALITY rather than coverage** — everything else adds fields or reach; this one makes an existing answer more trustworthy.
## Intention
🚨 **Every fingerprint hit is currently treated as equally exact.** We send a perceptual hash, get a match, and record it with no measure of how much to believe it. There is no trust signal anywhere in the pipeline.
The source publishes three, and we request none:
| Field | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `Fingerprint.submissions` | How many people independently submitted this fingerprint for this scene |
| `Fingerprint.duration` | The runtime the fingerprint was taken from |
| `Fingerprint.algorithm` | Which algorithm produced it |
## ⭐ D1 — Submissions is a crowd, and a crowd of one is not a crowd
A fingerprint submitted by forty people is a different claim from one submitted by a single person who may have mis-tagged their own file. 🔴 Today those are indistinguishable, and `MatchMethod.fingerprint` renders with a green seal — the app's strongest confidence signal — for both.
⚠️ **This is the failure shape this project keeps finding**: not a wrong answer, a confidently-presented one. A single-submission fingerprint wearing a green seal is exactly that.
## 🔴 D2 — Duration disagreement is the cheapest lie-detector available
We know the local file's runtime. If the fingerprint's duration disagrees materially, the match is weaker — and we can tell **without asking the source anything extra**, because the field rides along on a response we already make.
⭐ A hash collision or a mis-submitted fingerprint will usually show up here first. It is the single highest-value line in this spec.
❓ **Open — what tolerance?** Encodings differ by seconds; a different cut differs by minutes. Recommend flagging beyond a percentage rather than an absolute, and ⚠️ **reporting rather than rejecting** — a duration mismatch is a reason to look, not a verdict.
## D3 — Confidence is recorded, not just displayed
🔴 It belongs on the match edge, beside `method`. `MatchMethod` already encodes that the app knows some matches are stronger than others — it renders a seal or a question mark — and this makes that knowledge quantitative instead of categorical.
⚠️ Recorded at match time. The submission count moves as others contribute, so a number fetched later describes a different moment; without a timestamp it becomes a fact with no as-of, which is the mistake `marksAsOf` exists to avoid.
## ⚠️ D4 — It must not become an auto-reject
A low-confidence match is still very often right. 🔴 This surfaces doubt so a person can look; it never un-matches anything on its own. The same rule as upstream deletions, and for the same reason — the flag's meaning is not ours to interpret unilaterally.
## D5 — Algorithm is groundwork, not a feature
We send one algorithm and they read several. Storing which produced a hit costs nothing and is what makes multi-algorithm matching possible later. ⚠️ No behaviour today; a column and a comment saying why.
## 📊 Scale
1,378 videos carry an identity on the drive. Any of them matched by fingerprint currently has an unrecorded confidence. ❓ **Open:** is a backfill wanted, or does confidence start with new matches? Recommend the latter, matching *Source Descriptions* — prove the signal before spending 1,378 requests on it.
## Test strategy
- **C1** — A single-submission fingerprint is distinguishable from a heavily-corroborated one.
- **C2** — A duration disagreement is reported, and does NOT reject the match.
- **C3** — 🚨 Nothing is ever un-matched automatically.
- **C4** — Confidence is stored with the match, with an as-of, not recomputed for display.
- **C5** — A source supplying no fingerprint metadata leaves the match exactly as it is today.
- **C6** — A match made by title or cast is unaffected — this concerns fingerprints only.
